source.title: Data used in publications
source.description: Data used in preparation of article Resolving acoustic azimuth using an accelerometer-based underwater acoustic vector sensor

selection_protocol.reason: systematic beginning/middle/late positional sample from the 257-line published CSV after opening the source; selected without optimizing for coherence values
selection_protocol.exploratory_reason: noticed during source inspection because it contains a pronounced local coherence excursion; excluded from primary systematic summary

metric_boundary.interpretation: Published processed channel-coherence values from an underwater acoustic vector-sensor dataset.

exploratory_transient.information_gain: Real processed field data can contain strong local degradation even when neighboring windows are highly coherent; receiver/readback models therefore require time-varying channel-state awareness and should not equate detection with stable identifiability.

captain_obvious.primary_takeaway: A high-coherence ocean acoustic readback is neither constant nor sufficient by itself to identify the source.
captain_obvious.anti_cherrypick: The low 0.590055 point is explicitly exploratory because the row was noticed after inspection; it cannot be used as a preregistered primary effect.

relation_to_transceiver_model.supports: SEA/OCEAN ACOUSTIC FIELD -> VECTOR SENSOR -> PROCESSED COHERENCE READBACK is an actual engineered receive chain in field data.
relation_to_transceiver_model.does_not_support: The sea itself semantically decodes or stores messages as a database.
relation_to_transceiver_model.ba16_link: Even perfect measured coherence would establish observability, not recovery of provenance erased by a many-to-one forward map.

seal: FIELD COHERENCE CAN BE HIGH AND STILL VARY; OBSERVABILITY IS NOT IDENTIFIABILITY.
